odia: ଶତିକଈ ପୁରସ୍ତମ ଗଲା, ତୁଣ୍ଡ଼ କଥା କହି କହି ମଲା
title: A taunt that follows the speaker
literal_meaning: Shatikai went to Purastama and died talking and talking.
explanation: The repeated talking carries the taunt to an exaggerated ending. The dictionary explicitly marks Shatikai as a satirical feminine term for a lying or talkative woman; this is an insult, not a neutral portrait. Our reading follows how the verse makes speech swallow the whole journey. Its verbal energy can be appreciated while questioning its gendered target and refusing to treat women’s speech as an inherent fault.
meaning_odia: “କହି କହି”ର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତିରେ କଥା ଚାଲିଥାଏ, ଶେଷରେ ମରିବାର ଅତିରଞ୍ଜନ ଆସେ। ଅଭିଧାନ ଶତିକଈକୁ ମିଛ କହୁଥିବା ବା ବାଚାଳା ସ୍ତ୍ରୀ ପ୍ରତି ବ୍ୟଙ୍ଗଶବ୍ଦ ବୋଲି ଦେଇଛି; ଏହା ନିରପେକ୍ଷ ବର୍ଣ୍ଣନା ନୁହେଁ। ଆମ ପଢ଼ାରେ, ଯାତ୍ରାକୁ ପଛରେ ପକାଇ କଥା କହିବାଟି ସବୁକିଛି ହୋଇଯାଏ। ଧ୍ୱନିର ରସ ବୁଝିବା ସହିତ ନାରୀଙ୍କ କଥାକୁ ସ୍ୱଭାବଗତ ଦୋଷ କରୁଥିବା ଟାହିକୁ ମଧ୍ୟ ପଚାରିହୁଏ।
english_summary: A gendered taunt exaggerates relentless talking; our reading questions its target.
odia_summary: କଥାର ପୁନରାବୃତ୍ତି ରସ ତିଆରି କରେ, କିନ୍ତୁ ନାରୀଙ୍କୁ ଟାହିର ଲକ୍ଷ୍ୟ କରିବା ପ୍ରଶ୍ନଯୋଗ୍ୟ।
usage_example: Original imagined example: During a discussion of old sayings, someone quotes this line about a woman who speaks at length. Another listener enjoys the repeated sound but asks why the criticism singles out women. They discuss whether interruption, rather than gender, is the actual problem. No historic conversation is claimed.
